import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset

# Set the style of the visualization
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes

# Create a boxplot to show the distribution of transaction amounts by transaction type and fraud status
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', hue='is_fraud', palette='coolwarm')

plt.xlabel('Transaction Type')
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount')
plt.legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'])

# Save the figure

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set the style of the visualization
sns.set(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a boxplot to show the distribution of transaction amounts by transaction type and fraud status
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', y='amount', hue='is_fraud', palette='coolwarm')

# Add titles and labels
plt.title('Transaction Amounts by Type and Fraud Status')
plt.xlabel('Transaction Type')
plt.ylabel('Transaction Amount')
plt.legend(title='Fraud Status', loc='upper right', labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
